claims.claim: Perkins tells adventure writers to put puns, little laughs and Easter eggs in their text, embedded naturally rather than forced.
claims.source: Chris Perkins on Writing your own Adventures (D&D Beyond, 2018-04-19, Todd Kenreck transcript)

claims.claim: Perkins warns against writing an adventure like a novel that dictates how each encounter must resolve; the text must survive unexpected choices and dice.
claims.source: Chris Perkins on Writing your own Adventures (D&D Beyond, 2018-04-19, Todd Kenreck transcript)

claims.claim: Perkins characterizes the original 1983 Ravenloft as economical in its writing yet rich in characterization, the model he expanded.
claims.source: Ex D&D boss Chris Perkins tells us why Strahd is the RPG's most successful villain (Wargamer, 2026-03-19)

claims.claim: Wyatt set out to recapture the welcoming, teaching tone of the 4e DMG that the 2014 DMG lacked.
claims.source: D&D's James Wyatt & Chris Perkins Talk 2024 DM's Guide (CBR, 2024-10-25)
claims.quote: the helpful tone to ease you in

claims.claim: Perkins found DMs did not know material existed in the 2014 DMG, so the 2024 text is organized to surface what is there.
claims.source: D&D's James Wyatt & Chris Perkins Talk 2024 DM's Guide (CBR, 2024-10-25)
claims.quote: they didn't even know it was there

claims.claim: Wyatt wrote the 2024 DMG's examples of play as scripts of the game unfolding to show how it functions.
claims.source: D&D's James Wyatt & Chris Perkins Talk 2024 DM's Guide (CBR, 2024-10-25)
claims.quote: presenting the scripts of that unfolding in play

claims.claim: The 2024 DMG front-loads basic information about DMing and moves world creation to the middle, mirroring the PHB's structure.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and James Wyatt Answer Burning Questions About the 2024 DMG, page 2 (EN World, 2024-10-25)
claims.quote: front-loading all of the basic information

claims.claim: Wyatt names the 2014 DMG's organization as its biggest drawback and says a DMG should guide you on how to be a DM.
claims.source: Chris Perkins and James Wyatt Answer Burning Questions About the 2024 DMG, page 2 (EN World, 2024-10-25)
claims.quote: the organization of the 2014 DMG was its biggest drawback

claims.claim: Every published WotC adventure opens by explaining what boxed text is; with the 2024 DMG defining it on p. 9, Wyatt wants to drop that boilerplate.
claims.source: After DM's Guide Preview, Future D&D Adventures Will Drop These Two Repetitive Features (Screen Rant, 2024-10-29)
claims.quote: tells you what boxed text is

claims.claim: Perkins says re-explaining doors in every adventure bothered him for a decade; the 2024 DMG's doors page lets adventures stop repeating it.
claims.source: After DM's Guide Preview, Future D&D Adventures Will Drop These Two Repetitive Features (Screen Rant, 2024-10-29)

claims.claim: Abadia (AL admin): dropping boxed text does not remove the need to tell the DM what to convey; the test is whether information reaches the DM.
claims.source: The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020 (Teos Abadia, Alphastream, 2020-02-20)
claims.quote: the DM still needs some way to understand what to convey

claims.claim: AL Season 8's rigid template scattered one animated door's description across Dimensions & Terrain, Door and Creatures/NPCs sections, obscuring intent.
claims.source: The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020 (Teos Abadia, Alphastream, 2020-02-20)

claims.claim: The AL 'Playing the Pillars' sidebars existed to exist and added little value.
claims.source: The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020 (Teos Abadia, Alphastream, 2020-02-20)
claims.quote: It exists sort of just to exist

claims.claim: Abadia finds the 2025 Monster Manual devotes far fewer words to describing monsters and less actionable encounter information than 2014's inspiring lore.
claims.source: Best and Worst of the Revised Monster Manual (Teos Abadia, Alphastream, 2025-03-13)
claims.quote: far fewer words devoted to describing the monster

claims.claim: 2025 Multiattack lines inconsistently include 'in any combination', and the gelatinous cube's codified wording is harder to understand than before.
claims.source: Best and Worst of the Revised Monster Manual (Teos Abadia, Alphastream, 2025-03-13)
claims.quote: a fair lack of clarity in monster stat blocks

verdicts.trueWording: Put puns in your adventure. Put little laughs. Put little Easter eggs.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the D&D Beyond transcript. Perkins: 'Put puns in your adventure. Put little laughs. Put little Easter eggs in your adventure.' The 'embedded naturally rather than forced' limb is carried by 'you don't have to go out of your way to be funny because the people around the table are going to bring that' and 'my favorites have little gems of humor embedded in them'.

verdicts.trueWording: write an adventure like a novel - you can't do that
verdicts.note: Claim carries no quote, so verbatim is not testable; substance fully supported. Page: 'It's very easy for somebody who's accustomed to reading novels to write an adventure write a novel and you can't do that because A; you don't know who the protagonists are... and B; this is a game with dice rolls and random outcomes.' Dice limb: 'your villain will get critical hit four times in a row and die before he even gets through a monologue... The adventure has to be able to withstand that'. Dictated-resolution limb: 'if... everything they encounter has to be solved in a certain way or they just can't move forward, that also feels very unrealistic and unrewarding.'

verdicts.trueWording: rich in such characterization, despite ... an 'economical' writing style
verdicts.note: Wargamer page: 'The original Ravenloft was rich in such characterization, despite (as Perkins calls it) an "economical" writing style.' 1983 dating present ('The original 1983 Ravenloft module'). Expansion limb: 'If I was going to dare expand the setting around Castle Ravenloft...' and 'it was Perkins' goal to stay faithful to the module's villain-first nuance, even as he built up the world around the original module's castle.'

verdicts.trueWording: the helpful tone to ease you in
verdicts.note: CBR, James Wyatt verbatim: 'the Fourth Edition DMG was so good at introducing people to the game, and it's very sad that the 2014 DMG wasn't as good. So, part of what I did... was to try and bring in some of that, not even so much as the content, but the helpful tone to ease you in to the amazing and wonderful world of dungeon mastering.' Note the page's 'wasn't as good' is slightly softer than the claim's 'lacked', but the teaching/welcoming and 4e-model limbs are explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: surfacing the information that's in the guide in a better way
verdicts.note: CBR, Chris Perkins verbatim: 'I'll be describing something that was in the 2014 DMG, and they didn't even know it was there... one of the things we talked about early on was just making sure that we're surfacing the information that's in the guide in a better way, so that people actually know it's there and can find what they're looking for.'

verdicts.trueWording: presenting the scripts of that unfolding in play
verdicts.note: CBR, Wyatt verbatim: 'I worked on the examples of play in both the Player's Handbook and the Dungeon Master's Guide, which to me are really strong introductions to what this game is, and how you play it. As a narrative exercise, it's all dialogue... and presenting the scripts of that unfolding in play, I think, is the answer to my eight-year-old self saying, "How is this a game?"' The page says 'worked on' rather than 'wrote', in an interview about the 2024 books.

verdicts.trueWording: front-loading all of the basic information about what DMing is
verdicts.note: EN World page 2, Perkins verbatim: '...keeping in mind what we were doing with the Player's Handbook and putting in the more instructional first chapter on how the game works. And making this feel like the mirror image of that book by front-loading all of the basic information about what DMing is or ought to be and saving the more creative stuff, the create your own world for the middle of the book.' All three limbs (front-loading, world creation to the middle, PHB mirror) explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: the organization of the 2014 DMG was its biggest drawback
verdicts.note: EN World page 2, Wyatt verbatim: 'I think everybody recognized that the organization of the 2014 DMG was its biggest drawback... Well, it's not a Dungeon Master's Guide if it doesn't guide you on how to be a Dungeon Master.' Both limbs are in one Wyatt answer.

verdicts.trueWording: having to explain what boxed text is in every adventure
verdicts.note: Raw page reached; the quoted string 'tells you what boxed text is' does NOT appear on the Screen Rant page (checked case- and whitespace-normalised over both HTML and extracted text). Substance holds in other words: 'James Wyatt has his own "stupid little thing" that's been irking him - having to explain what boxed text is in every adventure... the typical "Running the Adventure" section sticks an explanation inside an example'; p.9 limb: 'gets to boxed text just as quickly, explaining how it works on page 9'; wants-to-drop limb: 'Per Wyatt's preference, this explanation might serve as blanket coverage for future adventures, although he's not completely confident that the change will happen.'

Screen Rant verbatim: 'Having to explain doors in every published adventure has apparently been irking him for the past decade... addressing something adventurers encounter so often seemed "super, super important"'. Doors-page limb: 'the inclusion of a page on doors'; stop-repeating limb: 'The obvious implication is that future published adventures can leave the door explanations behind.'

verdicts.trueWording: the DM still needs some way to understand what to convey
verdicts.note: Alphastream verbatim: 'If you don't have boxed text, then the DM still needs some way to understand what to convey to the PCs.' Reach-the-DM limb: 'Boxed text... is only part of the way an adventure communicates what is happening to the DM, and through the DM to the players' and 'how all parts of the adventure format can help or hinder the DM'. The cited page carries no byline naming Abadia and does not state an AL-admin role; authorship (Teos Abadia) and organized-play credentials are confirmed on the same site's About page (alphastream.org/index.php/about-and-contact/), which lists AL adventure authoring/development and 'Lead Administrator for Ashes of Athas' rather than literally 'AL admin'.

Alphastream verbatim: 'We get a description of the door under "Dimensions & Terrain," but then we get a clarification under "Door"... But we can't just look at "Door." You must read both places.' Third section limb: 'the "Creatures/NPCs" section has information on when the door animates (within 5 feet) and what it says.' Season 8 / rigid template limb: 'Season 8 required that authors use the format'; obscuring limb: 'it actively obfuscates the content and makes the adventure harder to run well at the table.' (The worked example is a Moonshae CCC adventure written to the Season 8 format, not a WotC-authored AL module.)

verdicts.trueWording: It exists sort of just to exist, and doesn't add a ton of value
verdicts.note: Alphastream verbatim: 'The Playing the Pillars sidebar hits one of my pet peeves. It exists sort of just to exist, and doesn't add a ton of value.' The page discusses one instance of a format-mandated sidebar; the format generally is described earlier ('you might have "Playing the Pillars" to give DMs ideas').

verdicts.trueWording: far fewer words devoted to describing the monster
verdicts.note: Alphastream verbatim: '2024 seems to forget this, providing far fewer words devoted to describing the monster. The words we do find have less useful or inspiring information, particularly when it comes to actionable information for creating encounters.' 2014 comparison limb: '2014 is often mentioned favorably by DMs who were inspired by its lore.' Written in Abadia's own voice under his 'Needs Work: Loss of Lore' heading (he opens the section citing designer friends, then states the finding himself); the book is called the '2024/2025 Monster Manual' on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: a fair lack of clarity in monster stat blocks
verdicts.note: Alphastream verbatim: 'there is still a fair lack of clarity in monster stat blocks.' Inconsistent-Multiattack limb: 'Some monsters state Multiattack like the Bandit Captain: "The bandit makes two attacks, using Scimitar and Pistol in any combination." Other monsters are like the Behir... it appears the order is fixed, since it lacks the "any combination" wording seen in the Bandit Captain.' Cube limb: 'Gelatinous Cube has updated language that in attempt to codify what it means to be in the cube, ends up harder to understand.'
